solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American paving team go missing

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
informally, things that disappear are said to walk, as in 'my pen has walked'

explanation.surface: A road crew mysteriously fails to turn up for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go missing' is the informal sense of WALK, as when an unattended item 'walks'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a pavement or footpath beside a road is a sidewalk.

clue.text: A sudden surprise, missing hard blow

indicators.note: the surprise word lacks the pencil-grade letter

parts.note: a shock is a sudden upsetting surprise
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone gets an unexpected jolt when a heavy punch misses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sock is an informal word for a hard punch or blow.

clue.text: Party vote disrupted, Conservative getting in? It's for the birds!

parts.note: a do is an informal party

indicators.note: the abbreviation for Conservative goes inside the jumbled letters
a disrupted vote has its letters thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An election is disrupted as a Tory sneaks in; a cynic dismisses the whole thing as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the birds' is an idiom for worthless, but here it is literal. 'disrupted' rearranges VOTE to VEOT, and C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovecot is a structure housing pigeons or doves, so it is literally made for birds.

clue.text: Handy way to give the plot some fluidity?

definitions.text: Handy way to give the plot some fluidity?

parts.words: Handy way to give the plot some fluidity?
parts.note: plot sounds like a story line, but here it is a garden bed, and the fluidity is water carried by hand in a spouted vessel

explanation.surface: A writer seeks a convenient trick to make a story flow better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a novel; it is a garden plot, and 'Handy' means held in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener carries this spouted vessel by hand to pour water onto flower beds and vegetables.

clue.text: Hero seen around capitals of Spain, Bulgaria … and Portugal

indicators.note: the hero word is placed around the chosen initials

parts.note: a lion is a brave, celebrated person, a hero

indicators.note: capitals are the capital letters that begin Spain and Bulgaria

explanation.surface: A champion is spotted visiting the capital cities of three European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals of' gives SB, then does double duty for the definition: the capital of Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital city of Portugal, read here via the clue's earlier mention of capitals.

clue.text: Runs when piano produces rough sound

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
p is the musical marking for soft, piano

explanation.surface: A pianist hurries through a passage and the instrument grates.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh grating noise is a rasp, like that of a coarse file.

clue.text: Mark of excellence in trial phase

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words trial phase, straddling them

explanation.surface: A product earns top marks during its testing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial phase' hints at an alpha test, but the letters are spelt out across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in some marking schemes, as in alpha plus for outstanding work.

clue.text: Quality support given to tyre in need of repair

parts.note: a prop is something that holds another up

indicators.note: a broken tyre has its letters reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A garage props up a car whose tyre needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a characteristic or quality of a thing, such as hardness.

clue.text: Greatly want firm to take on old soldier

indicators.note: a firm taking on a recruit adds him to its staff, so the soldier joins on after the firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a vet is short for veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A company is eager to hire an ex-serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire something intensely, often what belongs to another.

clue.text: Article in horoscope is poor, being wrong about cold

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for cold
letters that are wrong are out of order, so the words is poor are to be rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses a newspaper horoscope as poor and inaccurate about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being wrong' rearranges IS POOR to SPOIRO... set as S-O-R-P-I-O, and 'about' wraps that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve star signs, each given its own entry in a horoscope column.

clue.text: No longer washing oneself, standing round about, panting

indicators.note: the phrase for having left the tub stands round the word for concerning

parts.note: someone who has finished bathing has stepped out of the tub
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone climbs from the tub and stands around gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing round' puts RE inside the phrase OUT OF BATH, between its B and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of breath after exertion is exactly what panting is.

clue.text: Bonnets, nonetheless, may be available here

definitions.text: Bonnets, nonetheless, may be available here

parts.words: Bonnets, nonetheless, may be available here
parts.note: a bonnet sounds like hat-shop stock, but on a car the bonnet covers the engine and the boot holds luggage, and at this kind of sale goods are sold from the back of cars

explanation.surface: Hats can be bought here after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonnets' suggests millinery; the joke is that a bonnet and a boot are both parts of a car, and a car boot sale is a British market where people sell second-hand goods from their car boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand bonnets, as headgear, might well turn up among the jumble sold from car boots.

clue.text: Top arrangement of music — something for Salad Days?

parts.note: a cap is a lid or top

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders, here reshuffling the letters of music

explanation.surface: A music critic praises the best arrangement of a score from the musical Salad Days.
explanation.walkthrough: Salad Days is a 1950s British stage musical, which explains the music; the definition reads it literally as days for salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum, the sweet pepper, is a common salad vegetable, so it suits salad meals.

clue.text: Operating cash, initially money held in silver

indicators.note: the following pieces are held inside the symbol for silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of cash only

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A business is running with funds kept in silver bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating cash' looks like a single phrase, but 'Operating' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone acting as manager is operating in that role temporarily, performing its duties.

clue.text: A measure of compensation for not participating in film?

definitions.meaning: something that counterbalances a loss, as in a tax allowance against earnings
an actor not filming is away from the set, read as two words

explanation.surface: An actor asks for payment for being left out of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset balances or cancels out a cost, so it works as compensation; separately, off set means away from where filming happens.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer, wary, and not entirely unyielding

parts.note: shy means cautious, wary

indicators.note: the strict word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: stern means strict and unyielding

explanation.surface: A lawyer is cagey yet only partly firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a slang term for an unscrupulous lawyer who uses dishonest methods.

clue.text: Scattered beams with energy

parts.note: spars are poles or beams, as on a ship's rigging
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Light rays are dispersed, full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' suggests light, but it means timbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse describes things thinly spread out, scattered rather than dense.

clue.text: Rescuers treated chap's artery

indicators.note: treated suggests surgery, which reworks the letters of chap's artery into a new order

explanation.surface: Paramedics deal with a man's damaged blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A group sent out to find someone missing is a search party, i.e. a team of rescuers.

clue.text: Article about professional gear for the cook?

indicators.note: the article goes round the short professional

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A magazine feature on a chef's professional kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a magazine piece; it is the grammatical article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is the protective garment a cook wears over clothes in the kitchen.

clue.text: Small fish circling a disturbance

indicators.note: the young fish surround the letter a

parts.note: fry are young, newly hatched fish

explanation.surface: Tiny fish swim round in a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy quarrel or brawl, a disturbance of the peace.

clue.text: Person investigating death finding embarrassing situation involving love

indicators.note: the awkward-spot word wraps round the tennis zero

parts.note: being in a tight corner is being in an awkward spot
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An investigator stumbles on an awkward romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner is the official who holds inquests into sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: Front removed from ceiling timber subsequently

indicators.note: the opening letter of the beam word is taken away

parts.note: a rafter is a sloping beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: A builder strips the front off a roof beam.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, after means later on, at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Excavation belonging to the writer

definitions.meaning: a pit dug for coal or ore
the setter as writer says 'my own' with this possessive

explanation.surface: A crossword setter claims ownership of a dig site.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit for extracting coal is an excavation; the same word is the first-person possessive pronoun.

clue.text: Greatly upset about hot, sleepy condition

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation for hot
upset letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is very distressed about the heat making them drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greatly' looks like an adverb on 'upset', but it is the anagram fodder; 'upset' rearranges it to LETARGY, and 'about' wraps that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a state of drowsiness, sluggishness and lack of energy.
